title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu tammikuussa – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots en Route
content:
Plants have always travelled – with the wind, with animals and birds, with humans. They have been carried across oceans, taken from their habitats and replanted to serve trade and empire.

Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Äärilämpötilat ovat erityisen vaarallisia ihmisille, joilla yhdistyvät vakava sairaus ja sosiaalinen huono-osaisuus
content:
A Finnish–British study drawing on data from more than 285,000 individuals has found that global warming may lead to a further rise in temperature-related mortality.

“The health effects of extreme temperatures are often studied at the population level, but the risks are not shared equally. Our results show that the people at greatest risk are those who both have a serious medical condition and are socially disadvantaged. Identifying this group could help us target protective measures against extreme temperatures more effectively than before,” says Professor Mika Kivimäki of the University of Helsinki’s Faculty of Medicine and the Finnish Institute of Occupational Health.

The researchers compared mortality at typical temperatures with mortality at extreme temperatures, defined as the hottest or coldest 2.5% of all time periods. Follow-up lasted from 7 to 17 years.

title: Kahdeksan Helsingin yliopiston tutkijaa on maailman siteeratuimpien joukossa omilla aloillaan
content:
Eight University of Helsinki researchers have been named on the annual Highly Cited Researchers list. Five of the listed researchers have the University of Helsinki as their primary affiliation, while three work primarily elsewhere. Mika Kivimäki is included in two different categories.

The selected researchers have demonstrated significant and broad influence in their fields of research. The Highly Cited Researchers list recognizes researchers whose publications have been cited most frequently by other researchers over the past 11 years. 

Thousands of researchers are listed every year, and the list focuses on researchers in the natural and social sciences. The Highly Cited Researchers list, compiled by the analytics company Clarivate, is based on articles found in the Web of Science database.

title: Climate University as Highly Commended at the International Green Gown Awards 2026
content:
We are proud to announce that Climate University is a winner in the in the category of Next Generation Learning and Green Skills by receiving the Highly Commended award! 

When four HEIs in Finland started planning a joint climate course in 2014, it could not be foreseen that a decade later the scope at which the network operates would cover almost all Finnish universities and most of the universities of applied sciences, and that that the network would be an important stakeholder in making sustainability education accessible to students. The Climate University has evolved from an initiative of a few higher education institutions into a community of dedicated teachers, originating from different disciplinary backgrounds, but united by dedication to teach sustainability related Climate University courses to their students. These teachers are interested in growing professionally, exploring new ways of teaching and making sustainability education accessible to their students.  Climate University has also enabled other initiatives, like Specialisation programme in climate expertise (2024-), Climate University for Virtual exchanges Erasmus+ project for students from Ukraine (2023-2026), Una Europa Micro-credential in Sustainability (2022-), Climate change Teachers Academy (2022-), and many others.

title: Koronatartunnat eivät selitä lasten diabetespiikkiä koronasulkujen aikana
content:
Rates of type 1 diabetes among children rose in several countries during the pandemic lockdowns. Researchers have debated whether the SARS-CoV-2 virus was directly responsible or whether other factors were at work.

“Our study shows that the sharp spike in type 1 diabetes during the lockdown in Finland levelled off and then clearly declined as soon as society reopened and the restrictions were lifted,” says doctoral researcher Susanna Tall of the University of Helsinki’s Faculty of Medicine.

Researchers at the University of Helsinki found that the incidence of type 1 diabetes in children fell by 15% in the first 16 months after the Covid-19 lockdowns ended. This decline followed directly on from the lockdown phase, during which incidence had increased by a comparable 16%. 

Antibody tests on blood samples also showed that many of the children who developed diabetes after the lockdown had previously been infected with the coronavirus, yet cases still declined.

title: Call for Papers – Seminar: Urban Research in Biological and Environmental Sciences
content:
We invite all researchers to submit presentation proposals for the research seminar Urban Research in Biological and Environmental Sciences, which will take place on December 11, 2026, at the University of Helsinki. The aim of the seminar is to explore urban issues and cities from the perspectives of various branches of biological and environmental sciences and to offer a multidisciplinary forum for researchers engaged in urban studies.

Urban research is a central aspect of disciplines in the biological and environmental sciences, including urban ecology, environmental science, and conservation biology. Urban spaces shape ecosystems, biodiversity, and the living conditions of both humans and other organisms. The seminar will focus on the following three themes:

  • Biodiversity – Species, habitats, and ecological diversity in urban environments
  • Pollution and environmental quality – Contaminants, air and water quality, and their effects on organisms and ecosystems in cities
  • Environmental Change – Environmental pressures and adaptation in urban spaces, such as climate change, pollution, and land-use change
